newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IPO VIEW - H-share IPOs to beat 96 record in first half.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW - H-share IPOs to beat 96 record in first half.

text.p: A record number of H-share IPOs is set to hit Hong Kong this year, with more Chinese companies expected to list shares in the territory in the first half alone than in all of record-setting 1996, analysts said.
Investors are keen to snap up China-related stocks as they anticipate improvements in China's economy -- and Chinese businesses are expected to take advantage of the demand.

"The number of H-shares will definitely be more than in 1996, with more Chinese enterprises trying to tap strong sentiment for red chips and H-shares," said Kelvin Tang, analyst at Impac Asset Management.
H-shares are Hong Kong-listed shares of China-incorporated firms, while red chips are Hong Kong companies with China ties.

Consultancy Arthur Andersen said this week that about 40 Chinese enterprises are queuing up to launch initial public offerings (IPOs) in Hong Kong. It said H-share issues generally raise more than HK$200 million each.
"I believe that the number of H-share listings this year will exceed the record in 1996," partner Kennedy Liu said.
"H-share listings are likely to represent a significant portion of the total funds being raised in IPOs for the whole year," he said, adding that he sees about 30 to 50 IPOs in 1997.
Andersen worked on three H-share listings in 1996. Liu expected the firm to do seven or eight over the next two years.
Market sources said they expected about five H-share listings in the first quarter and at least two in the second quarter compared with six H-share listings in 1996.

Analysts said investor response to the issues should be better than last year, when the H-share index lagged the blue chip Hang Seng index for most of the year but then staged a strong year-end rally to close 1996 with a 30 percent gain.

A recent surge in China B shares and red chips has improved sentiment towards the sector, with investors anticipating that further interest rate cuts in China should boost corporate earnings, analysts said.
B shares are mainland-listed shares in Chinese companies available only to foreign investors.

"Upcoming H-share flotations are expected to enjoy a relatively better response due to two main factors -- a better macro-economic picture in China and better fundamentals at the listing candidates," said William Lo, Head of China Research at Kleinwort Benson Securities (Asia) Ltd.
Analysts said infrastructure issues were likely to be among the most promising this year due to the Chinese government's drive in that area.
Among upcoming issues, China Eastern Airlines is planning a dual listing in New York and Hong Kong. Its IPO is expected to begin sometime this month followed by China Southern Airlines.

Analysts said foreign investors generally have very limited opportunities to directly participate in China's transport, infrastructure and telecommunications businesses and may want to participate through initial public offerings.

Jiangsu Ninghu Expressway Co Ltd, one of 38 domestic firms recently selected by China as a candidate for an overseas listing, and Shenzhen Freeway are also expected to kick off their IPOs in first quarter.

China Aviation Technology Import & Export Corp's Shenzhen branch is expected to seek a listing in the second quarter and Datang Power's delayed dual listing plan in Hong Kong and London is expected to get back on track soon.
Market sources said toll road operator Zhejiang Huhangyong Expressway is also plannning a listing later in June.
